facts.detail: The page was published on 6 October 2017.
The consultation closed on 10 November 2017.
The statement was published on 1 March 2018.
Ofcom describes broadband as an essential service for people and businesses.
Customers need realistic speed information at point of sale and in their contract.
Existing codes require signatories to provide likely speed estimates.
The codes include a penalty-free exit if speed falls below a minimum level.
Major broadband-speed code changes took effect in March 2019.
The changes added a minimum guarantee and peak-time expectations before sign-up.
The live-sync estimate deadline was extended to 13 December 2020.

facts.detail: The automatic-compensation guide was published on 12 March 2024.
The page was last updated on 20 July 2026.
Compensation amounts increase each year in line with inflation.
Delayed-repair compensation begins when service is not fixed after two full working days.
The listed delayed-repair amount is £10.34 per calendar day.
The listed missed-appointment amount is £32.31.
The listed delayed-start amount is £6.46 per calendar day.
The scheme covers all residential fixed broadband and landline products of signatories.
Compensation should generally be credited no later than 30 days after resolution or the relevant event.
For loss of service, the customer reports the fault and payment becomes automatic if repair exceeds two full working days.

facts.detail: The automatic-compensation statement page was published on 24 March 2017.
The consultation closed on 6 June 2017.
The page status is Statement Published and closed.
Ofcom concluded that an automatic compensation scheme was needed for residential consumers.
Delayed repairs following loss of service are within the scheme scope.
Delayed installations are within the scheme scope.
Missed appointments are within the scheme scope.
The statement sets out how the scheme should be implemented.
The decision introduced a transparency General Condition for SME service-quality information.
The 1 April 2021 revision specified annual inflation-linked increases to compensation amounts.

facts.detail: The switching-broadband guide was published on 4 August 2010.
The page was last updated on 1 July 2026.
One Touch Switch requires the customer to contact only the new provider.
The process tells customers about applicable early termination charges.
Customers provide the services, address and current-provider details to the new provider.
The current provider sends information to help the customer decide whether to proceed.
The new provider arranges the switch date where possible.
The old service ends automatically once the new service is working.
Any loss of service should not last longer than one working day.
Customers have a 14-calendar-day right to cancel the order.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer rights, contract protections and service-quality processes do not establish physical network availability, exact parcel orderability or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: The provider-failure guide was published on 13 February 2026.
Where another company takes over, service should usually continue without interruption.
The existing contract should usually transfer to the new provider.
If the new provider changes terms, the customer should be able to exit without an early termination charge.
Customers unhappy with the replacement provider can switch.
If no company takes over, service will stop on a stated date.
The customer must sign up with a new provider to continue service.
The customer should not have to pay early termination charges in the no-takeover scenario.
It may not be possible to keep the existing phone number.
Vulnerable customers should tell their provider so additional support can be offered.
